title: Client Rapid Intake Playbook — First 8 Weeks
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, operational playbook for new customer onboarding focused on rapid intake, activation, and stabilization across the first 8 weeks. It is intended for mid-market and enterprise customers who are moving from trial or POC to committed usage. Use this when a customer needs a compact, high-velocity onboarding plan that balances engineering enablement with measurable adoption experiments.

Principles:
- Time-to-value first: identify the 1-2 features that deliver immediate value and instrument them as activation events.
- Fail fast, instrument more: short experiments each week with clear success thresholds.
- Shared responsibility: CS owns adoption, Solutions/SEs own technical enablement, Eng owns blockers and higher-risk integrations.
- Keep the customer in control of pacing; provide recommended checkpoints but be flexible.

Success metrics (examples to pin in CRM):
- Activation events: first successful API call with production model, first successful embedding index creation, first user-visible response within SLA.
- Time to first meaningful response: target <72 hours for hosted API, <7 days for Dedicated initial setup.
- Weekly active routes (unique endpoints used) >= 2 by week 6.
- Latency SLO met on 90th percentile for baseline tests by week 8.
- Renewal signals: usage >= 60% of committed capacity by month 3 or explicit product ROI evidence.

Week-by-week plan (high level):
Week 0: Intake + kickoff
- Deliverables: intake form completed, access granted, initial success criteria agreed, stakeholders and escalation path confirmed.
- Tasks: create project in CRM, open onboarding Jira CS-<id> ticket, invite SE and SRE leads to kickoff.
- Owner: CS lead for the account.

Week 1: Fast path demo + sandbox validation
- Deliverables: sandbox demo with customer data sample or synthetic dataset; first API key and test run.
- Tasks: run a smoke test script, capture token-level cost estimate, note model pins to recommend.
- Experiment: A/B two prompt variants to see latency/quality tradeoffs.

Week 2: Integration runway
- Deliverables: basic integration (server-side or client) making authenticated requests, sample scorecard populated.
- Tasks: share postman collection or SDK snippets, troubleshoot CORS/networking, collect telemetry.
- Risk check: confirm no private network constraints for Dedicated.

Week 3: Quality tuning + evals
- Deliverables: small eval harness with 50 prompts, quality baseline recorded, thresholds documented.
- Tasks: recommend quantization profile if cost is a concern; flag any hallucination patterns.

Week 4: Observability and cost guardrails
- Deliverables: dashboard access to Console for slowest routes, cost alerts configured, token quotas recommended.
- Tasks: set up tracing hook, add customer to rollouts for latency experiments.

Week 5: Early production cutover (canary)
- Deliverables: canary route receives low % of traffic, rollback plan in place.
- Tasks: run throughput tests, validate KV cache benefits for repeated prefixes.

Week 6: Scale plan + performance tuning
- Deliverables: autoscaling policy draft for Dedicated or usage-based alerts for Hosted.
- Tasks: apply batching recommendations, finalize model and quantization profile for steady state.

Week 7: Adoption experiments and training
- Deliverables: two adoption experiments live (email nudges, feature flags), internal enablement session recorded for product team.
- Tasks: handoff material to customer success manager.

Week 8: Stabilization + renewal prep
- Deliverables: adoption dashboard review, renewal health check, consolidated runbook for production operations.
- Tasks: schedule QBR, propose next quarter goals, collect NPS/feedback.

Risk ledger (quick):
- Networking blockers: Private/VPC peering delays. Mitigation: request network diagram at intake, early SRE sync.
- Data compliance: customer wants on-prem model. Mitigation: map to Private deployment path and timeline as a contingency.
- Cost surprises: unexpected token volumes. Mitigation: daily cost sampling and token caps in first 2 weeks.

Templates and snippets (drop-in):
- Intake checklist: legal contacts, technical lead, expected throughput, allowed data types, security contacts, compliance requirements.
- Sample kickoff agenda: 15m intros, 30m success criteria + milestones, 30m technical constraints and next steps.
- Sample activation email (to customer):
  Subject: Redwood onboarding: access + first steps
  Hi team,
  Quick summary: your sandbox is ready, API key attached, and we recommend starting with the smoke test in the attached Postman collection. Goal this week: confirm the first successful response. If you hit any blocker ping #cs-onboarding or reply here.
  Thanks,
  Aisha + SE

Notes to self / CS playbook tips:
- Keep weekly 30m syncs only if there is active work; otherwise switch to async updates in the shared doc.
- Track activation events in CRM as milestones; that helps trigger Solutions compensation and supports renewal narratives.
- Use the Console retention view to call out regressions during model rollouts.

Handover checklist to Renewal:
- Document at least three customer outcomes tied to product usage.
- Show trending usage vs commit and identify risks.
- Collect one internal quote and one customer testimonial snippet.

Open questions / backlog items:
- Add a standard quick-start for Dedicated capacity bump requests (JIRA template).
- Small automation: create auto-generated daily cost digest for new accounts in first 14 days.
- Integrate a templated eval harness into onboarding repo (see github PR link above).

Related artifacts and refs:
- Confluence onboarding intake template: confluence:cs/onboarding-intake
- Onboarding SDK snippets repo: github:https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-scripts
- Ticket for this account: JIRA:CS-772
- Slack channel: #cs-onboarding

Status and next edits:
- Draft as of 2024-11-27. Intended to be trimmed and converted into a one-page checklist and a 10-slide kickoff deck for enablement.

End of doc.
